title: Fattoush
subtitle: Levantine bread and vegetable salad with sumac dressing
excerpt: A Levantine salad of fresh tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, and herbs tossed with crisped toasted pitta and a sharp, tangy dressing of lemon, olive oil, and ground sumac.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fattoush is a salad from the Levant region (Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Palestine) and is one of the most widely eaten dishes in Levantine cooking. The name comes from fatteh, the Arabic word for crumbling, referring to the broken pieces of bread. Like the Italian panzanella, it is a bread salad designed to use stale flatbread, which is either fried in oil or baked dry until crisp before being added to the salad. The key seasoning is sumac, the dried, ground berry of the Rhus coriaria plant, which provides a fruity, tart, slightly astringent flavour that no other spice replicates.

content.text: The toasted pitta should be crisp rather than hard: bake it in the oven or toast it under a hot grill until very crisp but not burned. Add the pitta to the salad no more than 10 minutes before serving: longer and the dressing will make it soggy. The salad is better under-dressed than overdressed: sumac and lemon together are quite sharp, so dress lightly at first and taste as you go.

items.preparation: split open, baked at 200 C for 8 minutes until crisp, then broken into pieces

content.text: Make the dressing: whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, sumac, salt, and pepper.
Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, red pepper, spring onion, parsley, and mint in a large bowl.
Add the crisp pitta pieces to the salad. Pour over the dressing and toss gently. Taste, adjust seasoning and sumac, and serve immediately.
